summary: Construct one-dimensional formal modules over the integers of finite extensions of Q_p, their logarithms, finite-height deformations and Lubin–Tate torsion characters. Compare with the existing arithmetic Artin map, prove the unramified Honda and supersingular elliptic comparison, and build marked quasi-canonical lattice quotients with their smallest quadratic ring-class fields. Both ramified and unramified CM extensions are included. The BKO specialization identifies tame and anticyclotomic towers and proves trace-compatible comparison maps.

nodes.title: Formal group homomorphisms
nodes.statement: For commutative rings R and commutative Mathlib formal laws F,G, a homomorphism is h∈XR[[X]] satisfying h(F(X,Y))=G(h(X),h(Y)). Hom(F,G) has pointwise G-addition; composition gives the endomorphism ring. An isomorphism has unit derivative and the existing substitution inverse; strict means derivative one. None of these conditions identifies the entire reduction with X.
proofSteps: Use substitution identities to prove closure under composition and formal addition, then construct the inverse by PowerSeries.substInvOfIsUnit.
Prove coefficient extensionality, tangent additivity/multiplicativity and coefficient base change. Preserve source and target laws in every substitution.
acceptance: The hom carrier coerces injectively to PowerSeries R; inverse identities are two-sided.
Strictness and a special-fiber marking are separately named predicates.

nodes.title: One-dimensional formal modules
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring A and A-algebra R, a one-dimensional formal A-module is a commutative Mathlib FormalGroup R and a unital ring homomorphism A→End_R(F) inducing the given A→R on derivatives. A-linear homs commute with every [a]. For A=O_K and a field k of residue characteristic, height h means the first nonzero term of [π] is cX^(q^h), c≠0; infinity means [π]=0. Heights of lifts are heights of their special fibers.
proofSteps: Build the action on the existing endomorphism ring, with the tangent equality a property of that action.
Over a field differentiate the homomorphism equation: zero derivative forces a p-power factorization. Commuting with residue scalars forces the exponent to be a q-power.
Use a unit change of π and an invertible coordinate to prove height independence, and form coefficient base change by mapping the action.
acceptance: No phantom action inferred from a rank label; morphisms intertwine actual series.
Restriction of coefficients O_F/O_0 of degree n sends height one to O_0-height n.

nodes.title: Adic formal-module points
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete separated linearly topologized commutative A-algebra and I an ideal defining an adic topology. For a formal A-module over R, form the newtype F(I) of parameters in I, with evaluated formal addition, inverse and A-action. Continuous coefficient maps carrying I into J induce continuous A-linear maps. In particular F(m_L) exists for every complete finite extension L/K and F(m_Kbar) is the union over finite extensions, rather than an unjustified evaluation on an incomplete algebraic closure.
proofSteps: Use the existing topologically nilpotent evaluation, not FormalGroup.Point, for each parameter in I.
Construct the inverse series degree by degree from F(X,Y)=X+Y+…, evaluate it, and prove the group and module identities by continuity of substitution.
Apply comp_eval₂ to coefficient maps and each variable of the multivariate law. Prove the identity-on-parameters equivalence with Tau Ceti elliptic adic points.
For algebraic torsion points evaluate in a finite complete extension containing their coordinates; prove independence under enlargement.

For a Dedekind adic-completion presentation, compose this identity-on-parameters equivalence with the pinned unconditional formalPointHomAdicCompletion. Reuse its injectivity and range theorem exactly in that presentation. For a general local field use the imported completion comparison; do not extend the pinned theorem by dropping its hypotheses.
acceptance: Agreement with the pinned elliptic point group is an A-linear equivalence, including addition and inverse.
Base change and coordinate transport commute, as do Galois actions and coefficient-fixed homomorphisms.

nodes.title: Normalized formal logarithm
nodes.statement: For a commutative formal law F over a characteristic-zero domain R with fraction field K, construct the unique logarithm ℓ_F∈XK[[X]], ℓ′(0)=1, satisfying ℓ_F(F(X,Y))=ℓ_F(X)+ℓ_F(Y). Its inverse is the formal exponential. For h:F→G, ℓ_G∘h=h′(0)ℓ_F, and hence ℓ_F∘[a]=aℓ_F. These are formal identities; integral coefficients and convergence of the exponential on the whole maximal ideal are not asserted.
proofSteps: Construct the invariant differential (∂F/∂Y)(X,0)^−1 dX by formal differentiation; integrate coefficientwise in K.
Associativity makes it invariant, so the integral is additive under F; tangent normalization gives uniqueness.
Use the existing substitution inverse for exp and deduce the homomorphism formula. Compare with EllipticCurves Layer 1 by uniqueness, not by a second elliptic logarithm.
acceptance: The elliptic comparison preserves its chosen parameter and invariant differential.
Coefficient embeddings and coordinate maps commute with the normalized logarithm after accounting for their derivative.

nodes.title: Lubin–Tate interpolation
nodes.statement: For admissible f,g for the same π and a finite list of coefficients a_i∈O, there is a unique integral multivariate series H with prescribed linear form Σa_i X_i and f∘H=H∘(g,…,g). Uniqueness also holds among series over K with that linear form. The construction is coefficientwise and commutes with isomorphisms of the input data.
proofSteps: Suppose H is solved below degree r≥2. The degree-r error is divisible by π because reduction sends f,g to Frobenius and residue coefficients satisfy a^q=a.
Correct it by division by π−π^r=π(1−π^(r−1)); the second factor is a unit.
Take the coefficientwise degree limit. Uniqueness over K follows from the nonzero scalar π−π^r. Use this uniqueness for all subsequent identities.
acceptance: The statement permits arbitrary finite arity; arity two constructs addition and arity one constructs homomorphisms.
No p-adic completeness is used for this coefficient induction.

nodes.title: Finite-height torsion comparison
nodes.statement: Let G be a one-dimensional formal O_K-module over a complete noetherian local O_K-algebra R, with residue characteristic p and finite special-fiber O_K-height h. For m≥1, R[[X]]/([π^m]_G) is finite free of rank q^(hm) and its formal Hopf law defines a finite locally free group scheme. The levels are the π-power torsion of a connected p-divisible group in R07.1, whose p-height is h[K:Q_p]. Coefficient base change and coordinate isomorphisms identify these actual group schemes.
proofSteps: The reduction of [π^m] has order q^(hm). Apply pinned Weierstrass preparation and its quotient equivalence; monicity gives the stated free basis and rank.
Descend the formal addition and action to the quotient algebra and use the existing finite locally free group-scheme carrier.

Prove the π-level exact sequences by finite flat division, and compare the p-power cofinal subsequence using p=unit·π^e. Apply R07.1’s connected formal/p-divisible equivalence, rather than a second definition.
acceptance: Ranks are q^(hm) at π-level m and p^(h[K:Q_p]r) at p-level r.
The level m=0, when used, is the trivial group scheme of rank one.

nodes.title: Formal-module Tate module
nodes.statement: Over the integers of a finite extension L/K of characteristic zero, let G have O_K-height h. The π-adic inverse limit T_πG of geometric π-power torsion with transition [π] is free of rank h over O_K, and T_πG/π^m identifies with G[π^m](Lbar). The action of G_L is continuous and O_K-linear. Its underlying Z_p-module canonically identifies with the R07.1 Tate module of the associated p-divisible group, using the unit correction between π^e and p. The torsion module is (T_πG⊗K)/T_πG.
proofSteps: In characteristic zero the finite levels are étale and [π] is surjective on geometric points. Use exactness and the elementary divisor theorem over O_K to obtain (O_K/π^m)^h.
Lift a basis compatibly along the surjective transitions, take inverse limits, and compare cofinal p- and π-systems with their units.
Derive torsion identification, continuity and functoriality; base change L→L′ restricts the Galois action without changing the geometric module.
acceptance: A chosen basis is used only to display a matrix representation; the module and its Galois action are intrinsic.
For h=1, automorphisms are scalars, so the resulting character is basis independent.

nodes.title: Lubin–Tate division fields
nodes.statement: For F_f over O_K and m≥1, its primitive π^m-torsion consists of the O_K/π^m-module generators. For any generator t_m, K(t_m)=K(F_f[π^m]) is totally ramified of degree (q−1)q^(m−1). The action identifies its Galois group with (O_K/π^m)× and sends t_m to [a]t_m. Consecutive generators can be chosen with [π]t_(m+1)=t_m.
proofSteps: For the standard series πX+X^q, the first primitive point t_1 satisfies the Eisenstein polynomial π+X^(q−1), so it is a uniformizer of K(t_1). Given a uniformizer t_m, the polynomial X^q+πX−t_m is Eisenstein over O_(K(t_m)); a root t_(m+1) is again a uniformizer and satisfies [π]t_(m+1)=t_m.
Prove the primitive degree and total ramification inductively. The torsion action injects the finite Galois group into (O/π^m)×; equality follows from the computed degree.
Transfer arbitrary admissible f by the same-π coordinate isomorphism.

nodes.statement: For the marked deformation problem in LT.3 and every small Artinian extension R′→R, lifts exist.
